A: There he is. Alright? Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Alright.
A: So I've got to ask, it's saying Darren on mine. Are you Darren as well?
B: Yeah, Darren. They've stuck a B on me.
A: Ha, I'm A then. Where are you to?
B: Taunton.
A: You're joking. Me too, mate. North side, off the Kingston Road way.
B: I'm out the other edge, er, towards Bishops Hull sort of direction. Small world.
A: Small world, yeah. What d'you do, then? You've got a logo on there.
B: Duty manager down the leisure centre. Pool, gym, sports hall. I started as a lifeguard, what, twenty-five years ago, and just sort of never left.
A: Oh, I know it. Did the pool shut the other week? My partner was moaning she couldn't get her swim in.
B: Yeah, that was us. The boiler went, two days shut. Phones never stopped. People get very upset about their lengths, you know.
A: I bet. I'm at the builders' merchant out on the industrial estate, I run the branch. Trade counter, yard, couple of drivers. Eleven of us.
B: Right. I've probably been in. I'm doing up an old VW camper, been doing it for about four years.
A: Four years, that's nothing, mate. I've got a builder who's been nearly finished on the same extension for eight months. Comes in every Monday, "nearly done, Daz." He's not. To be fair he's a nice bloke, but he's not nearly done.
B: Ha. Sounds like my camper, to be honest.
A: Is it the Transporter, the T4, T5?
B: T4. Just got a new leisure battery fitted, so it's progress. Slow progress.
A: That's the way. I've got an old Honda moped in the garage, same thing, I just go and look at it really. What else do you do? Cricket?
B: Somerset, yeah, loosely. Get to the County Ground a couple of times a summer. Decent T20 season.
A: Decent season, yeah. I go for the T20 nights mostly, bit of cider, bit of shouting. And I do skittles Thursdays. We lost by two pins last week, two pins.
B: I'm five-a-side Thursdays.
A: I used to play, till the knee went at about forty. Now it's just walking the dog up the Quantocks.
B: Same, I'm up there with ours most weekends. Jack Russell cross, Pip. She's going a bit deaf now.
A: Ours is a Border Terrier, Biscuit. He's eaten another sock this week, so I'm waiting to see where that turns up.
B: Ha. Lovely.
A: Hang on, let me guess: two Darrens, same town, same age probably, both dogs, both up the Quantocks. You're not with someone who works at a dentist, are you?
B: Er, yeah, actually. Claire's a dental receptionist.
A: No way. Nicola's a practice manager at one. Which surgery?
